name: Appendicitis red flags
description: Belly pain with certain patterns may mean appendicitis, which needs imaging and urgent evaluation. This is not a diagnosis. Only a clinician with blood tests and imaging can confirm it.
time_criticality: Hours to days — the risk of rupture increases with time

citations.text: Mayo Clinic. Appendicitis: symptoms and causes.
Wagner JM, McKinney WP, Carpenter JL. Does this patient have appendicitis? JAMA. 1996;276(19):1589-1594.

validated_population: Not a validated score. Validated appendicitis scores (such as Alvarado) need blood tests. This pattern uses the classic findings reviewed in the JAMA Rational Clinical Examination series.
self_report_note: No home check can rule appendicitis in or out. Children, older adults, and pregnant people often have atypical symptoms.
license_note: Pattern logic and question wording are original to OLA BOT, based on the public guidance cited. Not a validated scoring instrument.

red_flags.question: Is your belly hard like a board, or too painful to touch or move at all?
red_flags.help: A rigid belly can mean a burst appendix or other emergency.

items.question: Where is your belly pain right now?
items.help: Point to where it hurts most.

options.label: Lower right side (between hip bone and ribs)

items.question: Did the pain start around your belly button and then move to your lower right side?
items.help: This shift is a classic sign of appendicitis.
items.trace_label: Pain moved from belly button to lower right

items.question: Do you have a fever?
items.help: 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, or feeling feverish with chills.

items.question: Are you vomiting or unable to keep food or liquids down?
items.help: Throwing up, or unable to keep down even sips of water.

items.question: How bad is the pain on a scale of 1 to 10?
items.help: 1 is barely noticeable; 10 is the worst pain you can imagine.

items.question: When did the pain start?
items.help: Your best estimate of when the belly pain began.

items.question: Do any of these apply? (Select all that apply)
items.help: Leave all unchecked if none apply.

options.label: Lower-right pain that feels hard or lumpy
Signs of shock (dizziness, rapid heartbeat, pale skin)

scoring.pattern_text: HIGH suspicion: (lower-right pain OR pain that moved there from the belly button) AND (fever OR vomiting) AND moderate-to-severe pain. MODERATE suspicion: lower-right or belly-button pain that is moderate-to-severe. Otherwise LOW.
scoring.threshold_text: Pattern check, not a score. Routing: signs of shock → call 911; other complication signs, moderate-to-severe lower-right pain, pain migration, or fever with vomiting and moderate-to-severe pain → emergency department today; moderate-to-severe belly-button pain → urgent care or ED today; mild pain within 24 hours → primary care today.

levels.label: Pattern: HIGH suspicion for appendicitis
levels.interpretation: Your symptoms raise significant concern for appendicitis.

levels.label: Pattern: MODERATE suspicion for appendicitis
levels.interpretation: Your symptoms could represent appendicitis, but other conditions are also possible.

levels.label: Pattern: LOW suspicion (not typical of appendicitis)
levels.interpretation: Your symptoms do not match the typical pattern of appendicitis.

steps.label: Severe belly swelling, very high fever, or hard lower-right lump
Pain moved from belly button to lower right
Fever and vomiting with moderate or severe pain
Mild pain that started within 24 hours
Moderate or severe pain elsewhere in the belly

call_911.label: Emergency: signs of shock
call_911.interpretation: Dizziness, a rapid heartbeat, or pale skin with belly pain can mean internal bleeding, a burst appendix, or severe infection.

care.where_detail: Call 911. Lie down while you wait.
self_care: Do not eat or drink anything until you are examined (you may need surgery).

ed_today.label: Pattern suggests possible appendicitis: go to the ER today
ed_today.interpretation: Appendicitis is a surgical emergency. You need imaging (ultrasound or CT) and evaluation by a surgeon. The risk of rupture increases with time, and a ruptured appendix is dangerous.
ed_today.recommendation: Go to the emergency room today for evaluation and imaging.

care.within: Today (go now if pain is getting worse)
care.where_detail: Hospital emergency department with ultrasound or CT and a surgeon on call.
ed_redirect: Signs of shock (dizziness, rapid heartbeat, very pale skin): call 911
self_care: Do not eat or drink anything until you are examined (you may need surgery).

urgent_or_ed.label: Belly pain needs same-day evaluation
urgent_or_ed.interpretation: Your symptoms could represent appendicitis, but other conditions are also possible.
urgent_or_ed.recommendation: See urgent care or go to the emergency room today. Depending on findings, you may need imaging.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic that can do blood tests and imaging, or an emergency department. Call ahead.
ed_redirect: Signs of shock (dizziness, rapid heartbeat, very pale skin): call 911
Pain moves to the lower right side: go to the emergency department
self_care: Do not eat or drink anything until you are examined (you may need surgery).

urgent_today.label: Belly pain needs same-day evaluation
urgent_today.interpretation: Your pain is not in the typical location for appendicitis, but moderate or severe belly pain needs same-day evaluation to find the cause.
urgent_today.recommendation: See urgent care or an emergency department today.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic, or emergency department if pain is severe or worsening.
ed_redirect: Signs of shock (dizziness, rapid heartbeat, very pale skin): call 911
Pain moves to the lower right side: go to the emergency department

primary_today.label: Mild belly pain: see primary care today
primary_today.interpretation: Your symptoms do not match the typical pattern of appendicitis. Early appendicitis can start mildly, so new belly pain should be checked.
primary_today.recommendation: See your primary care clinician today. Call ahead to explain your symptoms.

care.where_detail: Primary care same-day appointment. Urgent care if no same-day appointment is available.
ed_redirect: Pain worsens or moves to the lower right side

primary_soon.label: Mild belly pain: see primary care soon
primary_soon.interpretation: Your symptoms do not match the typical pattern of appendicitis.
primary_soon.recommendation: Book a primary care visit within 1 to 2 days, sooner if pain worsens.

care.where_detail: Primary care clinic or telehealth visit.
ed_redirect: Pain worsens or moves to the lower right side
